To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a design-driven validation framework is proposed to assess the confidence in making a design choice based on Bayesian prediction models, and that the proposed framework can be used to assess the validity of the Bayesian prediction models when the validation data are limited and the design domain is unknown.
a Bayesian approach can be used to validate a model for a specific purpose, and that the Bayesian approach can also be used to develop a model that is validated for a specific purpose.

(1) Bayesian prediction model can be developed for a design problem, which can provide the discrimination of design alternatives; (2) the uncertainty quantification based on the Bayesian prediction model can help to assess the confidence in the decision of using the Bayesian model in making a design choice; (3) the decision validation metrics are applicable to both discrete and continuous design problems; (4) the proposed approach is demonstrated through a robust design problem of engine piston.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of a model in a design context.
a new paradigm in model validation.
the development of a design-driven validation framework, in which the validation is based upon the ability to discriminate between competing designs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed design-driven validation approach provides a new perspective to model validation and can be a valuable tool in design under uncertainty.
the Bayesian approach is a powerful framework to develop the prediction model for design, and the proposed metrics can be used to assess the model validity from a design perspective.
the proposed approach provides an effective framework for validating the model in the design domain, and it has the potential to be applied to many engineering design problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a good model should not only be accurate, but also be capable of providing a good discrimination between design candidates.
the Bayesian prediction model is a better representation of the physical system than the deterministic model.
, in order to validate a model for design purpose, it is not sufficient to simply verify that the model accurately predicts the design objective at a limited number of test points.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bayesian approach can be used to develop a prediction for the design objective under uncertainty.

, in the context of design optimization, the validation of a computer model can be achieved by examining the uncertainty quantification of a Bayesian prediction model and its ability to discriminate between design candidates under uncertainty.
a good model is not just a good predictor, but also a good decision maker.
